claims: The Rooney Rule is an NFL policy established in 2003.
The Rooney Rule is named after former Steelers owner Dan Rooney.
The Rooney Rule requires teams to interview minority candidates for head coaching, senior football operation, and executive positions.
Teams must interview at least two minority candidates for head coaching vacancies.
Teams must interview at least one minority candidate for senior operational roles (e.g., General Manager).
Teams must interview at least one minority candidate for offensive assistant positions.
The Rooney Rule has expanded over time to include women and a broader range of positions, including quarterback coaches.
In 2022, the Rooney Rule was expanded to require at least one ethnic minority or woman on the offensive coaching staff.
Failure to comply with the Rooney Rule can result in significant fines from the league.
Critics, including coaches like Brian Flores, argue that teams often interview minority candidates only to fulfill the requirement rather than to seriously consider them for the position.
As of 2026, the Rooney Rule is facing legal threats, with claims that it constitutes illegal race-based discrimination.
